prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: 16:9 technical blog cover, new scene for a post about comparing Unreal Engine PIE client and server values in one process.
Input images: Image 1 is the Steady Spiral character identity reference. Image 2 is only the clay material, lighting and rendering style reference; do not copy its envelopes, numbers, paths or question mark.
Primary request: A curious Steady Spiral snail examining two side-by-side miniature game-world viewports inside ONE shared rounded desktop monitor, visually comparing two positions of the same player. The monitor and main snail form one compact central scene. Each viewport contains a small version of the exact same snail avatar on an identical simple ground track; one avatar is slightly further along the track than the other. This is a visual metaphor for locally reading client and server copies of the same player, not a network transfer diagram. A simple slim comparison rail below the two viewports has two rounded position pegs at slightly different positions. No numeric measurements.
Style/medium: polished soft clay-like 3D illustration, tactile matte surfaces, rounded simple props, warm ivory seamless background, soft studio illumination and gentle grounding shadows, matching Image 2.
Character invariants: dark deep-green plump body, lime spiral shell, two round thick antennae, ivory oval eyes and tiny friendly mouth; retain Image 1 silhouette, face proportions and recognizable identity. Main snail sits at the foreground of the shared monitor, looking thoughtfully at both viewports, without covering the avatars.
Composition/framing: wide 16:9 landscape, all meaningful subjects, main face, the entire two-viewport monitor and comparison pegs tightly grouped within the middle 50% of image width and middle 65% of height. Generous empty ivory margin on both sides and top/bottom; works in centered square and landscape crops and small mobile cards. Large readable forms, restrained details.
Constraints: exactly one shared monitor frame, two equal viewports, same avatar identity in both, small position mismatch. No cables connecting separate machines, no packet arrows, no speed joke, no assertion that values always match. No text, no title, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no watermark, no extra decorative scenery.

corrections.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit
Asset type: 16:9 blog cover, composition correction for severe center cropping.
Input images: Image 1 is edit target, Image 2 is original character identity reference, Image 3 is clay-rendering style reference.
Primary request: Revise the scene composition in Image 1 so the comparison is fully legible in a very narrow centered portrait crop. Keep the same clay style, ivory backdrop, Steady Spiral character identity and concept of reading two copies of one game player within ONE shared monitor. Change the monitor to a COMPACT upright monitor with two horizontal world viewports STACKED VERTICALLY, upper and lower, not side by side. Center the complete monitor at x=50%, from approximately y=40% to y=80%, and make its whole width only 22% of the wide canvas. Place the main snail directly BEHIND the monitor so its large friendly face and two antennae rise above the screen at x=50%, approximately y=22% to y=43%; lime shell visible beside the head. Do not obscure either viewport.
Each viewport shows a miniature same-identity snail on the SAME simple straight beige track, seen side-on. The top avatar is a little further along the track than the lower avatar. No clouds or foliage; give the two avatars clean uncluttered sage backgrounds. This is a metaphor, not a literal Unreal editor screenshot. No comparison rail below is needed.
Composition: landscape 16:9. Face and BOTH complete viewports must fit inside x=39%..61% of the entire image, y=22%..80%. Most of the canvas on the left and right is empty warm ivory studio space. The scene may look small in the wide full image; this is intentional for thumbnail-safe composition. Face is large relative to compact monitor. Shell and body can extend slightly outside this central stripe but core comparison and face cannot.
Invariants: original deep-green plump snail, lime spiral shell, two thick rounded antennae, flat ivory eyes and tiny ivory mouth; soft tactile matte clay, warm gentle studio light and contact shadows. One shared monitor frame, two views of the same player at slightly different positions. No text, no title, no labels, no letters, no numbers, no arrows, no watermark, no cables, no envelopes, no extra props.
